pages.lesson:
LESSON: WRITING 5.3.1 CREATIVE WRITING: CREATIVE LANGUAGE

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 5
Topic 5.3: Writing 5.3.1 Creative Writing: Creative language

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Writing 5.3.1 Creative Writing: Creative language. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: How do we develop good handwriting?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify aspects of creative language in texts based on the theme for fluency
2. write texts based on the theme neatly and legibly for effective communication

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

• Writing 5.3.1 Creative Writing: Creative language makes your writing clear so others can read it easily.

• Look at the model your teacher shows. Notice shape, order, and spacing.

• Practise slowly first, then build neat speed.

• Check your work: Did you spell carefully? Did you use correct marks?

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: Copy three model sentences neatly, leaving finger spaces between words.

Example 2: Spell five lesson words aloud, then write them without looking.

Example 3: Fix this sentence by adding capital letters and a full stop: “amina went to kisumu”

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Write five neat sentences about your school using words from this topic.
2. Exchange books with a friend and check spelling or punctuation together.
3. Rewrite one messy sentence so it is clear and correct.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Complete a short guided paragraph in your exercise book.
2. List eight words from this topic and practise spelling them with a parent.
3. Write a short note to a friend using correct punctuation.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Discuss the use of creative language in writing: proverbs, metaphors, saying and similes,
2. Read sample compositions online and offline to identify creative language,
3. Creativity and Imagination: This is developed as the learner exchanges ideas that inspire creativity when composing own compositions neatly and in good handwriting.
4. Digital Literacy: This is cultivated as the learner interacts with technology to read sample compositions online and offline to identify creative language. 30 Values:
5. Unity: This is cultivated as the learner teams up to create a collection of proverbs, similes, sayings and metaphors from texts.

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Neat writing helps the reader.
2. Check spelling and punctuation before you finish.
3. Practice a little every day.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
